steps.action: Chose established geomorphic indices (Smf, SL with a fixed 100 m ΔH, HI, AF, T on third-order dendritic basins) and data sources (1:50,000 toposheets, ASTER DEM, satellite images, limited fieldwork), with chi-square and Curray p tests.
steps.quote: The data were collected from Survey of India toposheets on 1:50,000 scale, ASTER DEM, satellite images, and through extensive field work.

steps.action: Mapped drainage anomalies and landforms: entrenched meanders, a hair-pin bend, Iril palaeochannels, a shutter ridge with wind and water gaps, a possible sag pond, and two-level terraces. Fault-controlled origins were offered as the most plausible reading, and terrace differences were left to complex response.
steps.quote: The higher-order streams in many reaches show such features as entrenched meanders, defeated streams, straight course, and sharp deflections

steps.action: Computed Smf for 108 mountain-front segments, SL for stream segments grouped into modal classes, and HI for 125 basins, then mapped their spatial distributions by thrust sheet.
steps.quote: the modes of SL being 219 in the Thoubal-Chandel thrust sheet and 140 in the Churachanpur-Mao thrust sheet

steps.action: Regressed HI against basin area to check for a basin-size control.
steps.quote: In other words, the basin areas have not influenced their HIs.

steps.action: Computed AF for 125 basins, translated it into azimuth classes per thrust sheet, and tested the class frequencies with chi-square against a random distribution.
steps.quote: testifies that the stream migrations in this part of Churachanpur-Mao thrust sheet have indeed been preferentially northward

steps.action: Regressed AF deviation against basin area.
steps.quote: In other words, the AFs are not dependent on basin areas.

steps.action: Regressed T magnitude against basin area.

steps.quote: the relatively higher values of HI and SL also suggest faster uplift of the leading edge of Thoubal-Chandel thrust sheet

end.claim: Both adjacent thrust sheets are actively uplifting by oblique slip at different rates: faster uplift in the north of the Thoubal-Chandel sheet tilts it southward, and faster uplift in the south of the Churachandpur-Mao sheet tilts it northward.

decisive_move.sentence: Without the AF chi-square and T vector-mean statistics of the 125 third-order basins, which give opposite preferential shifting directions for the two thrust sheets, the opposite-tilting claim would not exist.

gates.evidence: A similar-versus-dissimilar framing is stated (p. 665), but the data are generic indices on all accessible basins, not acquisition directed by it. The chi-square and Curray tests could have shown random shifting, and the confounder regressions could have shown dependence (pp. 676-679). The tilting mechanism, though, is attributed by elimination, not by a discriminating test. Thresholds (Smf classes, p<0.5, ΔH 100 m) come from the literature, but nothing says they were fixed before the data were seen.

novelty_claims.quote: its structural and active tectonic aspects have not yet been studied
The present investigations have provided insights into active tectonic aspects of a hitherto unstudied part of the Manipur Hills.

limits: Fieldwork was restricted by inaccessibility and insurgency, so most data come from toposheets and satellite images (p. 667). Fault splays near the shutter ridge were not observed (p. 675). There is no dating, so uplift is relative and no rates are given. Terrace elevation differences were left ambiguous (complex response, p. 676). Uniform lithology and climate are asserted, not measured; only drainage density was tested as an erodibility proxy. The chi-square tables, degrees of freedom and Curray computations are not shown in full. Sub-claims: faster relative uplift of the Thoubal-Chandel leading edge is estimate_with_resolution (relative only, no uncertainty); oblique-slip movement on the basal thrusts is best_explanation from landform assemblages; the general statement about adjacent thrust sheets (conclusion iii) rests on one case and is untested. No peer-review file was supplied. The acknowledgment that R.T. Cox and others improved the paper suggests, by inference only, that some checks may have been requested in review, but none can be attributed. The text extraction drops the signs of some r values (e.g. 0.16 is described as negative).
